content.value_statement: Discrete-event systems are hard to model without clear process and resource patterns. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create SimPy simulations with monitoring and analysis workflows.
actual_capabilities: Provides SimPy starter patterns for environments, processes, events, and shared resources.
Guides queue, producer-consumer, priority, preemptive, and parallel workflow simulations.
Includes reusable Python templates for customer-server simulations and resource monitoring.
Explains monitoring methods for wait time, utilization, queue length, and event history.
Supports CSV export examples for simulation metrics after a run.
Documents real-time simulation setup with SimPy real-time environments.
limitations: It does not replace statistical validation or domain-specific model calibration.
It focuses on SimPy discrete-event models, not continuous differential equation simulations.
Generated simulations still need testing against known cases and real operational data.
CSV export examples write only when the user calls the export helper.

use_cases.title: Plan Service Capacity
use_cases.description: Model customer arrivals, service times, staff capacity, wait time, and throughput before changing operations.

use_cases.title: Simulate Production Lines
use_cases.description: Represent machines, buffers, maintenance interruptions, priority work, and utilization metrics in a repeatable model.

use_cases.title: Prototype Research Models
use_cases.description: Create event-driven experiments for queues, resources, synchronization, and stochastic process behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Queue Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SimPy skill to create a simple queue simulation for customers, one shared server, arrivals, service time, and wait metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Add Resource Monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SimPy monitoring patterns to add queue length, utilization, wait time, and a short report to my existing simulation.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Capacity Scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SimPy skill to compare several resource capacities and summarize throughput, average wait, and utilization tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Model Priority and Interruptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use SimPy preemptive resources and process interaction patterns to model priority jobs, interruptions, recovery, and performance metrics.

output_examples.input: A clinic wants to test two, three, and four reception desks with random arrivals.
output_examples.output: A scenario plan with SimPy processes, shared reception resources, monitored wait time, utilization, and a comparison table.

output_examples.input: A factory needs to study machine downtime and priority repair tasks.
output_examples.output: A preemptive resource model design with maintenance interruptions, resumed work, utilization tracking, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: A network team wants to model packets competing for limited bandwidth.
output_examples.output: A discrete-event model outline with packet arrivals, bandwidth resources, queue metrics, latency statistics, and experiment parameters.

best_practices: Set random seeds and record all model assumptions before comparing scenarios.
Validate simple cases against expected results before adding complex process logic.
Track metrics throughout the run, including wait time, queue length, utilization, and throughput.
anti_patterns: Do not use blocking Python sleep calls inside SimPy processes.
Do not compare scenarios without consistent random seeds or equivalent input data.
Do not treat simulation output as a forecast without calibration and sensitivity analysis.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps build SimPy discrete-event simulations for queues, resources, events, monitoring, and capacity planning.

faq.question: Does it run simulations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates that users can run in their own Python environment.

faq.question: Can it model continuous systems?
faq.answer: It is best for event-driven systems. Use other scientific tools for continuous differential equation models.

faq.question: What metrics can it help collect?
faq.answer: It covers wait time, queue length, utilization, throughput, resource events, and container levels.

faq.question: Is it useful for capacity planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare resource capacities, arrival patterns, service times, and operational constraints.

faq.question: Does it need external services?
faq.answer: No. The examples use local Python and SimPy, with optional local CSV output for metrics.
